quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Tunde's neighbourhood looks after itself in small ways. When Mrs. Bello was ill, three neighbours brought her meals every day for a week. When the bus shelter broke, one man repaired it with his own tools, and nobody asked for thanks.
options: The neighbourhood has a rule that everyone must help.
A neighbour repaired the bus shelter using his own tools.
Mrs. Bello was ill for a week and needed meals.
People in Tunde's neighbourhood help each other without being asked.
quests.correctAnswer: People in Tunde's neighbourhood help each other without being asked.
quests.hint: When a paragraph gives examples, ask what general point they all illustrate.
quests.explanation: The meals and the repaired shelter are two examples of one idea: neighbours helping without expecting thanks. Either example alone is too narrow to summarise the paragraph.
keyPoints: Tunde's neighbourhood is full of small acts of help.
Neighbours fed Mrs. Bello while she was ill.
One man fixed the bus shelter and did not ask for thanks.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Wanjiru's market stall shows that good service can matter more than low prices. She remembers her regular customers' names and keeps their favourite fruit aside each week. Her prices are slightly higher than the stall next door, yet her line is always longer.
options: Friendly service can win customers even when prices are higher.
Wanjiru remembers the names of everyone in the market.
Wanjiru sells cheaper fruit than the stall next door.
Wanjiru saves her best fruit for customers who pay her more.
quests.correctAnswer: Friendly service can win customers even when prices are higher.
quests.hint: Compare the scope of each option with what the paragraph actually says.
quests.explanation: The paragraph argues that personal attention brings customers even when prices are a little higher. Options that reverse the price comparison or exaggerate her memory go beyond the text.
keyPoints: Wanjiru's stall is more popular than the one next door.
She remembers regular customers and saves their favourite fruit.
Her prices are higher, but service keeps her line long.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Dev's grandfather never wastes anything. He turns old jars into pencil holders, cuts worn shirts into cleaning cloths and plants herbs in cracked cups. Visitors are always surprised, because nothing leaves his house until every possible use has been found.
options: Dev's grandfather cannot afford to buy anything new.
Dev's grandfather sells his pencil holders to curious visitors.
Dev's grandfather finds second uses for old things.
Dev's grandfather grows herbs in cracked cups and old bowls.
quests.correctAnswer: Dev's grandfather finds second uses for old things.
quests.hint: Cross out options that describe one of several examples.
quests.explanation: Jars, shirts and cups are all examples of one habit: giving old things a second use. The wrong options either pick one example or add a reason the paragraph never gives.
keyPoints: Dev's grandfather is careful never to waste things.
He reuses jars, shirts and cups in new ways.
Nothing leaves his house until every use has been found.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Uma planned the community garden opening for months. She arranged the flowers, borrowed chairs and wrote a short speech. On the day, two hundred neighbours came, and the mayor cut the ribbon while the children planted the first seeds.
options: The mayor planted the first seeds in the new garden.
A community garden opened before a crowd of neighbours.
Uma borrowed chairs and wrote a speech for the opening.
Uma spent months arranging flowers for her neighbours.
quests.correctAnswer: A community garden opened before a crowd of neighbours.
quests.hint: Decide whether the paragraph is mainly about the getting ready or the event itself.
quests.explanation: The planning explains what came before, but the paragraph builds toward the opening day and the people who came. Choosing preparation details or misplacing the seed-planting misses the event.
keyPoints: A new community garden was officially opened.
Uma had planned the event carefully for months.
Two hundred neighbours attended, and children planted the first seeds.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Luca studied maps and shadowed a senior officer for two weeks before starting as a ferry dispatcher. On his first solo morning, fog delayed three ferries. He rebooked forty passengers calmly, and his manager praised him at lunch.
options: Three ferries were delayed by fog on Luca's first morning.
Luca spent two weeks studying maps before starting work.
Luca's manager promoted him to senior officer after the fog.
Luca's careful training helped him handle a foggy first morning.
quests.correctAnswer: Luca's careful training helped him handle a foggy first morning.
quests.hint: Look for how the early sentences connect with the later ones.
quests.explanation: Preparation and the test on the first morning are joined by the successful result, and the praise shows it worked. The other choices each stop at one stage of the story or invent a promotion.
keyPoints: Luca trained carefully before becoming a ferry dispatcher.
On his first morning, fog delayed three ferries.
He rebooked forty passengers calmly and was praised.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The school prepared for months to welcome visiting students from Japan. Classrooms were decorated, host families were chosen, and a schedule of trips was printed. When the visitors arrived, they were delighted, and several host families still write to them.
options: Classrooms were decorated for the students from Japan.
A schedule of trips was printed for the host families.
A school's careful planning made its visitors feel welcome.
Host families write to the visitors because of a school rule.
quests.correctAnswer: A school's careful planning made its visitors feel welcome.
quests.hint: Ask what all the preparations were for and how things turned out.
quests.explanation: The preparations, from decorations to trips, led to delighted visitors and lasting contact. A list of preparations without their outcome does not summarise the paragraph.
keyPoints: The school planned for months to host visitors from Japan.
It prepared classrooms, host families and trips.
The guests were delighted, and some families still write to them.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The fire drill at Hartley Primary took less than four minutes. Teachers led each class to the field, and older children helped the little ones. Ms. Ncube, the head, thanked everyone and said the school was well prepared.
options: Teachers led all the classes to the school field.
The school plans to hold a fire drill every week.
Hartley Primary completed a fast, well-organised fire drill.
Ms. Ncube thanked the older children for helping.
quests.correctAnswer: Hartley Primary completed a fast, well-organised fire drill.
quests.hint: Ask whether an option covers the whole school's response or one person's part.
quests.explanation: Teachers, older children and the head all played a part in a drill that went quickly and smoothly. Any single role is too narrow to summarise it.
keyPoints: Hartley Primary held a fire drill that took under four minutes.
Teachers guided classes and older children helped younger ones.
The head thanked everyone and said the school was well prepared.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: At Sunday's football match, Ruth scored twice, but the coach said the win belonged to the whole team. The defenders stopped every attack, the midfield passed carefully, and the goalkeeper saved a late shot. Ruth agreed and bought the team ice cream.
options: The goalkeeper saved a late shot in the match.
The whole team, not just Ruth, earned Sunday's win.
Ruth won the match by scoring twice on her own.
The defenders and goalkeeper played better than the midfield.
quests.correctAnswer: The whole team, not just Ruth, earned Sunday's win.
quests.hint: Sometimes the paragraph itself corrects an obvious idea. Notice whose view the coach and Ruth share.
quests.explanation: Ruth's goals are the obvious story, but the coach and Ruth both credit the whole team. Making Ruth or the goalkeeper the hero shifts the emphasis away from what the paragraph says.
keyPoints: Ruth scored twice in Sunday's football match.
The coach said every part of the team contributed to the win.
Ruth agreed and celebrated by buying ice cream for everyone.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Yusuf organised the office recycling scheme, but he says it works because everyone joins in. Staff separate paper and plastic at their desks, the cleaners collect bins each evening, and the manager reports the results monthly. Last month, waste fell by a third.
options: The manager has decided that staff must stop using plastic.
Waste fell by a third because Yusuf worked extra hours.
Yusuf collects all the office bins by himself each evening.
An office recycling scheme is working thanks to shared effort.
quests.correctAnswer: An office recycling scheme is working thanks to shared effort.
quests.hint: Check whether an option gives one person credit for what many people do.
quests.explanation: Staff, cleaners and the manager each do a part, and the result is a drop in waste. Options crediting Yusuf alone or inventing a plastic ban distort who did what.
keyPoints: Yusuf started the office recycling scheme.
Staff, cleaners and the manager all take part.
Waste fell by a third last month.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The library now closes the children's section for a short break each afternoon. Staff use that time to tidy books and clean tables. Parents were unhappy at first, but the section now looks fresh when it reopens at four.
options: The children's section reopens at four o'clock.
Staff close the section because few children visit it.
A daily closure keeps the children's section tidy.
Parents are still unhappy that the children's section closes early.
quests.correctAnswer: A daily closure keeps the children's section tidy.
quests.hint: Ask why a rule exists. The answer often appears in the middle of the paragraph.
quests.explanation: The break has a practical purpose: tidying and cleaning. The reopening time is a detail, and the parents' first reaction has since changed.
keyPoints: The children's section closes for a break each afternoon.
Staff use the time to tidy books and clean tables.
It reopens at four looking fresh, though parents first disliked the change.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Employees at the print shop must wear gloves when handling chemicals. The rule started after a worker had a skin reaction last year, and no similar problem has happened since. Managers also give a short safety talk to every new starter.
options: The print shop protects workers with gloves and safety talks.
Print shop workers handle chemicals during every hour of work.
New starters must give a safety talk to the managers.
A worker was dismissed after having a skin reaction last year.
quests.correctAnswer: The print shop protects workers with gloves and safety talks.
quests.hint: Search for the reason behind a rule, then choose the option that includes it.
quests.explanation: A past accident explains the rule, and the safety talk shows the shop's wider concern. Options that reverse who gives the talk or overstate the work invent facts.
keyPoints: Workers at the print shop must wear gloves with chemicals.
The rule began after a worker had a skin reaction.
Managers also give safety talks to new employees.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Cyclists must switch on their lights after sunset in this city. Police say most night accidents involve riders that drivers cannot see. Shops near the station sell lights cheaply, and officers hand out free ones during the first week.
options: Police hand out free lights to drivers throughout the year.
Shops must sell lights cheaply once the sun has set.
Cyclists have most of their accidents near the station.
The city requires bike lights at night to prevent accidents.
quests.correctAnswer: The city requires bike lights at night to prevent accidents.
quests.hint: A rule and its reason go together. Which option keeps both?
quests.explanation: The lights are required because unseen riders are involved in accidents, and the cheap and free lights help people comply. The wrong options change who receives lights or where accidents happen.
keyPoints: Cyclists in the city must use lights after sunset.
Police say unseen riders are involved in most night accidents.
Cheap and free lights are available to help riders follow the rule.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Nikhil's laptop was so slow that he sometimes missed online class deadlines. A friend suggested deleting old programmes and adding more memory. After both changes, the laptop started in half a minute, and Nikhil has not missed a deadline since.
options: Nikhil sped up his slow laptop and stopped missing deadlines.
Nikhil's friend deleted all of his old programmes.
The laptop now starts in half a minute without extra memory.
Nikhil bought a new laptop to replace his slow one.
quests.correctAnswer: Nikhil sped up his slow laptop and stopped missing deadlines.
quests.hint: Track the problem, the fix and the change in the result.
quests.explanation: The slow laptop caused missed deadlines, two fixes sped it up, and the deadlines are now met. Wrong options replace the solution or drop half of it.
keyPoints: Nikhil's slow laptop made him miss online deadlines.
He deleted old programmes and added more memory.
The laptop now starts faster, and he no longer misses deadlines.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The smartphone app kept logging users out, and customers filled the support line with complaints for two weeks. Developers found that the login code expired after five minutes. They extended it to an hour, and the complaints dropped sharply.
options: The support line was closed after two weeks of complaints.
Customers stopped using the app because of the busy support line.
Developers fixed a login problem by lengthening sessions.
Developers made the login code expire faster to protect users.
quests.correctAnswer: Developers fixed a login problem by lengthening sessions.
quests.hint: Sort the paragraph into problem, cause, action and result.
quests.explanation: The complaints came from a short expiry time, and lengthening it fixed the issue. Wrong options reverse the change or invent other outcomes.
keyPoints: An app logged users out and caused many complaints.
The login code expired after only five minutes.
Extending it to an hour reduced complaints sharply.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Bea's small online shop lost orders because the payment page failed on older phones. She hired a student to test the site on different devices. The student found the fault in one afternoon, and Bea's orders rose.
options: Bea's orders rose because she lowered her prices.
Testing phones helped Bea find and fix a payment fault.
Bea hired a student because her shop needed a new design.
Older phones stopped working after visiting Bea's online shop.
quests.correctAnswer: Testing phones helped Bea find and fix a payment fault.
quests.hint: Which option explains how the fault was found and what changed afterwards?
quests.explanation: The failing payment page reduced orders, testing revealed the fault, and fixing it brought orders back. The wrong options replace the cause or the reason for the recovery.
keyPoints: Bea's shop lost orders because payments failed on older phones.
A student tested the site on several devices and found the fault.
After the fix, her orders increased.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Sleeping less than six hours makes it harder to concentrate the next day. Tired people forget instructions, make more mistakes and react more slowly. A regular bedtime helps the body get the rest it needs.
options: A regular bedtime makes people react faster than usual.
Lack of sleep reduces alertness, so a routine helps.
Mistakes are the only sign that someone needs more sleep.
People who sleep six hours never forget instructions.
quests.correctAnswer: Lack of sleep reduces alertness, so a routine helps.
quests.hint: Separate the effect of a cause from the advice that follows.
quests.explanation: The paragraph links short sleep to poorer concentration and suggests a regular bedtime as a remedy. Wrong options exaggerate one effect or say the opposite of the passage.
keyPoints: Sleeping under six hours reduces concentration.
Tired people forget, make errors and react slowly.
A regular bedtime helps the body rest properly.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Walking to school helps children in several ways. They get exercise before lessons begin, and fresh air wakes them up. Teachers report that pupils who walk arrive calmer and pay attention more easily.
options: Children who walk arrive later than children who take the bus.
Fresh air is the only benefit of walking to school.
Walking to school gives children exercise and helps them focus.
Teachers ask children to walk because buses are unsafe.
quests.correctAnswer: Walking to school gives children exercise and helps them focus.
quests.hint: Ask what all the benefits have in common before you choose.
quests.explanation: Exercise and fresh air lead to calmer, more attentive pupils. The wrong options add unsupported claims about buses or lateness, or claim that only one benefit exists.
keyPoints: Walking to school benefits children in more than one way.
Exercise and fresh air help them wake up.
Teachers see calmer and more attentive pupils.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Drinking sugary drinks between meals can harm teeth. The sugar feeds bacteria, which produce acid that wears down the tooth's protective layer. Dentists suggest drinking water instead and saving sweet drinks for mealtimes.
options: Sugary drinks between meals damage teeth, so dentists advise water.
Bacteria in the mouth are fed only by water.
Dentists say sweet drinks are harmless at mealtimes.
Acid from bacteria protects the outer layer of a tooth.
quests.correctAnswer: Sugary drinks between meals damage teeth, so dentists advise water.
quests.hint: Follow the chain of cause and effect, then find the advice that comes from it.
quests.explanation: Sugar feeds bacteria, the bacteria make acid, and the acid harms the tooth, which is why dentists recommend water. The wrong options reverse a step or overstate the advice.
keyPoints: Sugary drinks between meals can harm teeth.
Sugar feeds bacteria, which make acid that wears away the tooth's layer.
Dentists recommend water and sweet drinks only at meals.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Every Thursday, Ximena visits her grandmother on the other side of the city. She takes two buses, carries fresh bread and stays for dinner. They talk about old photographs, and Ximena leaves with a full heart and a bag of leftovers.
options: Ximena travels across the city by two buses every day.
Ximena takes old photographs with her on the bus.
Ximena keeps a weekly tradition of visiting her grandmother.
Ximena's grandmother bakes bread for her Thursday visitors.
quests.correctAnswer: Ximena keeps a weekly tradition of visiting her grandmother.
quests.hint: Repeated details tell you what the paragraph is really about. What repeats here?
quests.explanation: The time, the journey and the dinner all describe one regular visit. Changing 'weekly' to 'daily' or switching who brings the bread misreads the details.
keyPoints: Ximena visits her grandmother every Thursday.
She travels by two buses and brings fresh bread.
They share dinner and talk about old photographs.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Wherever Samir travels, he asks locals where they eat lunch. He has found tiny kitchens behind bus stations and family cafés without signs. His notebook is now full of addresses, and friends ask him for advice before every trip.
options: Samir eats only in cafés that have no signs.
Samir finds local food by asking residents.
Samir's friends travel with him on every food trip.
Samir writes a food blog about the most famous restaurants.
quests.correctAnswer: Samir finds local food by asking residents.
quests.hint: Think about what Samir does every time and what he gets from it.
quests.explanation: His habit of asking locals leads to hidden places and a valued notebook. The wrong options add a blog, exaggerate the cafés, or change who travels.
keyPoints: Samir asks local people where they have lunch.
This has led him to hidden kitchens and small cafés.
Friends now ask for his advice before their trips.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: During exam season, Thandi studies in the same corner of the library at the same time each day. She puts her phone in her bag, sets a timer for forty minutes and takes a five-minute walk between sessions. She says the routine makes studying feel automatic.
options: Thandi walks for forty minutes between her study sessions.
Thandi leaves her phone at home during exam season.
Thandi enjoys the library more than she enjoys her home.
Thandi uses a fixed study routine to make revision easier.
quests.correctAnswer: Thandi uses a fixed study routine to make revision easier.
quests.hint: Find the sentence that gives Thandi's opinion, then judge which option reflects it.
quests.explanation: Place, time, timer and breaks form a routine, and the final sentence gives its purpose. Wrong options swap the times, change where the phone goes or invent a preference.
keyPoints: Thandi follows the same routine every exam-season day.
She studies in one place with her phone away and timed sessions.
She says the routine makes studying feel automatic.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Before signing a phone contract, compare the total cost over two years, not just the monthly price. Cheap plans sometimes include high set-up fees or limits on data. Reading the small print takes ten minutes and can save hundreds.
options: Cheap monthly plans are always the best choice.
Reading the small print will take hundreds of minutes.
Comparing the full cost of phone contracts can prevent expensive surprises.
Set-up fees are the only extra cost of a phone contract.
quests.correctAnswer: Comparing the full cost of phone contracts can prevent expensive surprises.
quests.hint: Test each option for words like 'always' and 'only'. Does the paragraph support them?
quests.explanation: The writer advises looking at the whole cost and the small print because low monthly prices can hide other charges. The wrong options turn 'sometimes' into 'always' and 'or' into 'only'.
keyPoints: Compare the total two-year cost of a phone contract.
Cheap plans can include fees or data limits.
Ten minutes of reading can save a lot of money.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: New drivers should practise parking in an empty car park before facing city streets. Slow, repeated attempts build confidence and help drivers judge the size of their car. Most instructors say a few hours of this practice makes real parking much less stressful.
options: Instructors say parking in cities is easy for new drivers.
Practising parking somewhere quiet helps new drivers feel more confident.
New drivers should avoid busy streets for their first year.
Empty car parks are the best place to learn every driving skill.
quests.correctAnswer: Practising parking somewhere quiet helps new drivers feel more confident.
quests.hint: Advice paragraphs have a suggestion and a reason. Find both.
quests.explanation: Practising in a quiet space builds confidence and judgment, which reduces stress later. The other options change the instructors' opinion or extend the advice to things not mentioned.
keyPoints: New drivers should practise parking in an empty car park.
Repeated attempts build confidence and a sense of the car's size.
A few hours of practice make real parking less stressful.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: If you are learning a language, listen to short recordings several times before moving on. The first time, you catch the general idea; later, you notice the small words and the rhythm. Teachers find that this repeated listening improves both understanding and speaking.
options: Teachers record their own speech to help learners listen.
Learners should move on to a new recording every time.
Small words matter more than the general idea in every recording.
Listening to the same short recording repeatedly builds understanding and speaking.
quests.correctAnswer: Listening to the same short recording repeatedly builds understanding and speaking.
quests.hint: Which option shows why the advice is useful, not just what it says?
quests.explanation: The advice to repeat recordings is supported by what learners notice each time and by teachers' results. The wrong options reverse the advice, over-rank one detail or add an unsupported teaching method.
keyPoints: Language learners should replay short recordings several times.
Each listening reveals more: first the idea, then small words and rhythm.
Teachers find it improves understanding and speaking.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Thirty years ago, Harbor Street had only fishing shops and a small market. As young families moved in, cafés, a bookshop and a music school opened. Today the street is busy in the evenings, though a few older residents miss the quiet.
options: Harbor Street is now quieter than it was before.
Older residents want the cafés and music school to close.
Harbor Street has become lively as new families arrived.
A bookshop was the first business ever opened on Harbor Street.
quests.correctAnswer: Harbor Street has become lively as new families arrived.
quests.hint: For change over time, compare how things were with how they are now.
quests.explanation: The street has moved from fishing shops to cafés and schools, and the atmosphere has changed with it. The wrong options invent an order of opening, exaggerate residents' feelings or reverse the change.
keyPoints: Harbor Street once had only fishing shops and a market.
Young families arrived and brought cafés, a bookshop and a music school.
The street is now busy, although a few residents miss the quiet.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When Ren started cycling to work, he could barely climb the hill near his house. Now, a year later, he passes the top without stopping. He has also lost some weight and no longer needs his car for short trips.
options: Ren sold his car so he could buy a better bicycle.
Cycling to work has improved Ren's fitness and changed his habits.
Ren lost weight because he changed his diet.
Ren still stops halfway up the hill near his house.
quests.correctAnswer: Cycling to work has improved Ren's fitness and changed his habits.
quests.hint: Look at the 'then' and 'now' in the paragraph. What links them?
quests.explanation: Regular cycling has changed Ren's strength and how he travels. Wrong options undo his progress, invent a car sale or credit a different cause for the weight loss.
keyPoints: Ren began cycling to work and found the hill very hard.
After a year, he climbs it without stopping.
He has lost weight and uses his car less.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: In the 1990s, most people in Deepa's town bought music on discs. Then downloads arrived, and now most listen through streaming apps. Small record shops have not disappeared, but their customers are mainly collectors who enjoy owning physical copies.
options: Collectors prefer downloads to owning physical copies of music.
Small record shops closed when streaming apps became popular.
Most people in the town still buy their music on discs.
Music habits changed, but record shops still serve collectors.
quests.correctAnswer: Music habits changed, but record shops still serve collectors.
quests.hint: A change over time often has a 'but' that adds an important qualification.
quests.explanation: The paragraph tracks discs, downloads and streaming, and adds that record shops survive by serving collectors. Wrong options say the shops disappeared, that discs are still the norm, or reverse what collectors like.
keyPoints: People in Deepa's town used to buy music on discs.
Downloads and then streaming became the usual way to listen.
Record shops survive by serving collectors of physical copies.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The local swimming club had too few coaches, so young beginners waited months for lessons. The club asked older members to train as assistant coaches and paid for their courses. Waiting lists soon shortened, and several trainees have since become full coaches.
options: Older members pay for their coaching courses by themselves.
A swimming club trained members as coaches to shorten waiting lists.
Beginners at the club still have to wait several months for lessons.
Several trainees became coaches at other swimming clubs nearby.
quests.correctAnswer: A swimming club trained members as coaches to shorten waiting lists.
quests.hint: Join the problem, the club's response and what happened next.
quests.explanation: The shortage of coaches caused delays, training members provided more coaches, and waiting times fell. Wrong options reverse the result, the payer or where trainees work.
keyPoints: The swimming club had too few coaches for beginners.
It trained older members as assistant coaches and paid for their courses.
Waiting lists shortened, and some trainees became full coaches.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The town's night market used to close in the rainy season because customers stayed home. Organisers built a covered walkway and added a small stage for musicians. Attendance is now steady all year, and traders say their income has become more reliable.
options: Cover and entertainment kept the night market open all year.
A covered walkway was built to protect the traders' stock.
The night market moved to another town during the rains.
Musicians now earn more than the traders at the market.
quests.correctAnswer: Cover and entertainment kept the night market open all year.
quests.hint: Which option covers both the changes made and the improvement they brought?
quests.explanation: Rain hurt attendance, the organisers responded with cover and music, and now the market runs all year. The wrong options misplace the beneficiaries, the location or the purpose of the walkway.
keyPoints: The night market used to close during the rainy season.
Organisers added a covered walkway and a stage for musicians.
Attendance and traders' income are now steadier all year.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ivan's family bakery wanted to reduce waste from unsold bread. In the evening, staff now sell leftover loaves at half price through a phone app. Most of the bread is bought within an hour, and the bakery saves money as well.
options: Bread is sold at half price only during the morning.
Staff eat the leftover loaves when the bakery closes.
A bakery reduces waste by discounting leftover bread.
The bakery throws away most of its bread every evening.
quests.correctAnswer: A bakery reduces waste by discounting leftover bread.
quests.hint: A goal, a method and a result: find all three in one option.
quests.explanation: Waste was the problem, discounted evening sales were the method, and the quick sales are the result. The wrong options reverse the outcome or change when and how the bread is sold.
keyPoints: Ivan's bakery wanted to waste less unsold bread.
Staff sell leftover loaves at half price through an app in the evening.
Most bread sells quickly, and the bakery saves money.
